messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — High error rate + elevated p95 latency for inference in az1a. Route: /v1/llm/generate. Affected customers: some Hosted tier requests. Docs: https://internal.runbooks.redwood/az-egress-degrade

maria: got the page, i'm oncall. seeing 502s and timeouts from hosts in az1a. metrics look like sudden TX packet drops on a subset of instances.

ajay: yep i'm pulling netflow now. BGP/route tables look fine, but ENI RX drops spiked at 14:02 UTC. Noticing unhealthy NLB targets for the g5-pool in az1a.

ops-bot: grafana snapshot: https://grafana.internal/s/az1a-inference/overview?from=now-30m to=now (link shortened)

maria: quick customer impact check — which models/routes are failing? Tanya?

tanya: our logs show model-batchers on az1a returning `connection reset by peer` during prefix fetch from kv-cache. Traffic to other AZs (az1b/az2a) unaffected. Canary traffic already routed to az1b.

li: CS: 3 active customers reported slow responses; two on Hosted API complaining about repeated 502s in last 8 minutes. Need ETA for mitigation to tell them.

ajay: isolation plan: 1) remove problematic targets from NLB in az1a 2) reroute new sessions to az1b 3) scale dedicated fallbacks in az1b by +30% for next 20m. Executing step 1 now.

maria: proceeding with step 1. Command: ``aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --targets Id=i-0abc1234``

ops-bot: target deregister started, health checks failing repeatedly on 8/12 hosts. Reaction +:maria: :thumbsup:.

ajay: health checks show `ENETUNREACH` and `ETIMEDOUT` from the host kernel logs. Looks like instance-level NIC soft error not full host OOM.

tanya: workaround: force traffic to model-variant-light (lower kv-cache memory pressure) for customers on Hosted while we stabilize. Update rollout policy: `/routes/*` prefer variant `v1-light` in az1a fallback.

maria: rolling canary redirect of 20% to az1b and applying variant fallback. Command snippet: ```curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/rollout -d '{"route":"/v1/llm/generate","canary":0.2,"fallback_variant":"v1-light"}'```

ajay: confirming autoscaler in az1b triggered, added 12 pods (g5-sim). Watch CPU/latency.

ops-bot: alert: downstream queue backlog dropping but p95 latency across global rose from 220ms -> 380ms briefly.

maria: customer comms draft: "We're investigating increased errors and latency for inference in one AZ. We've rerouted traffic and applied fallbacks; some requests may see slightly higher latency. We'll update in 15 minutes." Approve? @james-cs

james-cs: approve. please include list of affected endpoints and mention mitigation steps. Keep tone: technical but calm.

li: opening support ticket list and notifying top-5 customers via DM.

ajay: digging into instance telemetry: kernel logs show NIC firmware reporting `rx_drop` escalations correlated with a recent host kernel update at 03:05 local. Rolling back that kernel on a test host now.

tanya: if rollback fixes rx path, plan is to gradually bring targets back into NLB. If not, escalate to cloud provider.

maria: test host after kernel rollback shows RX drops reverted to baseline and health checks pass. Good sign.

ajay: start re-registering healthy hosts in az1a in small batches (3 at a time) with 2m wait for stability. Command: ``aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn ... --targets Id=i-0abc3456``

ops-bot: re-registering batch 1: 3 hosts healthy. batch 2: 2 failing, removed.

maria: continuing slow reintroduce. monitoring for packetdrop and kv-cache thrash.

tanya: keep variant fallback enabled for az1a routes for additional 30 minutes after full reintroduction to avoid regressions.

li: CS update sent to affected customers: confirmed reroute + temporary variant; ETA for normal ops ~+45 minutes.

ajay: provider ticket opened with AWS support referencing instance IDs and kernel signature; case #CASE-2026-9999. We'll include test results.

maria: summary for postmortem: single AZ instance NIC rx-drop after kernel update caused NLB target failures -> elevated errors/latency for inference routes. Mitigations: deregister bad targets, reroute to az1b, apply model-variant fallback, rollback kernel on test host, reintroduce hosts in controlled batches. Next steps: coordinate kernel rollout freeze, add NIC telemetry anomaly alert, update runbook with variant-fallback step.

tanya: +1 on runbook change. Need clear command snippets for model fallback and route rollout in runbook.

maria: handing off to followup oncall @ajay for remediation and PM to do comms. I'll stay on for 10 mins then shift.

ajay: taking followup. I'll monitor reintros and AWS case. ping me if errors spike.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (partial). Traffic normalized for majority of customers; monitoring for 30m.

maria: thanks all. I'll file postmortem template and include timeline.

james-cs: closing loop with CS: customers acknowledged. closing internal comms once postmortem posted. :white_check_mark:
